# NOTES ON TWO BOOKS (compact reference; not commentary)

## BOOK 1 of 2: "The B. O. W. C.: A Book For Boys" by Prof. James De Mille (Boston, Lee & Shepard, 1871; Gutenberg #56231). Dedicated "To Willie."

### Cast
- **Bart Darner**: fair, round-faced, merry, mischievous, curly golden hair; son of a St. John merchant; longs for sea; founder/genius of the B.O.W.C.; ran away twice (once found at inn ~40 miles off; second hid in woods with Solomon's help). Carries leather cup, pistol, sailor knife; made flag, red shirts, feathered hats; "Venerable Warden" costume. Poor sailor, bluffs about seamanship.
- **Bruce Rawdon**: elder Rawdon twin-like brother, big, brawny, Roman features, dark curling hair; "Most Venerable Patriarch" for May; heart trouble after cliff ordeal and "doldrum" spells.
- **Arthur Rawdon**: younger Rawdon, similar look; saved Bruce by holding Bart's leg-tree grip; grabbed rope at Antelope; killed shark with handspike; carved oar.
- **Tom Crawford**: tall, slight; found lobster; "stronger" paddler.
- **Phil Kennedy**: small, slight; built signal staff, sacrificed red shirt to wave at schooner; lost a boot in mud.
- **Solomon** (old African cook, "Old Solomon"): made "Perpetual Grand Panjandrum"; speaks dialect ("mos' wossifle"); bought turkeys, chickens, pies; later on the bank, "Wenebble" speech.
- **Dr. Porter**: head master of Grand Pré School; proposed schooner cruise.
- **Mr. Simmons**: mathematics teacher; mineral enthusiast; amiable, bachelor.
- **Mr. Long**: English dept.; energetic, rapid, stern; hard to soften; wanders to find boards; blew fog-horn; said "Jonahs"; later said "bother your baby"; walked off at Blomidon.
- **Captain Corbet** (Benjamin): skipper of schooner *Antelope*; neglectful; wife away, infant "babby" (said "Bo-rax," "Ga-ga"); lectured Bart that apostle Paul had a compass ("So we fetched-a compass"); cracked anchor.
- **Mrs. Corbet**: absent wife; "high-sperited creetur."
- **Mate (Mr. Wade)**: wife named "Gipson"; sleeps in barn; slow.
- **Bob/Jiggins/Pat etc.** — the voyageurs: **Pat (Michael Murphy/"Patsie")**: Irish, sky-blue coat; ate raw clams; ignorant (threw minerals in mud). **Johnnie Blue (Peter Fraser)**: bullet-headed, sailor-dressed. **Bogud (David Digg)**: studious, geology, pale; "David and Bogud are common." **Muckle (George McLeod)**: red soldier coat. **Jiggins (Jacob Wiggins)**: grave, earnest, red bandana; scratched clams; "my doubts." **Billymack (William MacNamara)**: tail coat, top boots. **Sammy Bam Ram (George Henderson)**: ragged; steward/cook with Johnny; stole pig.
- **Captain Pratt**: owner of Pratt's Cove; loud, hearty; sawmill; wood-pile.
- **Mrs. Pratt**: kindly; medicine chest (long list of remedies); clam poison lore ("In the months without the R").
- **Denny (Dennis) O'Rafferty**: Irish; five-fold Five Islands farm; son Michael died June 5, 1845 aged 15; wife Mary; hatchet gift with B.O.W.C. initials.
- **Old Blomidon** ("Blow me down").
- **Captain Kidd jest**; "Pinnacle Island."

### Places
Grand Pré School (Grand Pré, Nova Scotia), Minas Basin, Cornwallis River, Blomidon, Five Islands, Pinnacle Island, Gaspereaux (Gaspereaugians), Mud Creek, Parrsboro, Pratt's Cove, Spencer's Island, Horton Bluff, Ile Haute, Windsor, Cape Split, Cornwallis Bridge, Shubenacadie.

### Plot Sequence
1. I: Meeting in Rawdons' rooms (costumed white sheets; Solomon "Grand Panjandrum" audience). Flag with skull-like face and "B.O.W.C." = Brethren of the Order of the White Cross. Officers: Most Venerable Patriarch, Venerable Scribe, Right Worshipful Commander, Grand Scholastic, Venerable Warden. Bust = phrenological bust from medical student.
2. II: Procession in cart driven by Solomon; camp by brook at woods; damming; Dr. Porter offers schooner cruise round Minas Basin; no firearms (Bart keeps pistol).
3. III: Ragged crew procession; ballast stolen from garden wall (Mr. Brown's fence); Captain Corbet found feeding baby; sail off; flag raised by Bruce firing pistol.
4. IV: Blomidon; "Blow me down" etymology; songs ("Captain Kidd," blue-bottles, "Farmer's Boy"); seasickness; hats lost in squall; Five Islands; Pinnacle Island; landing.
5. V: Bruce goes over cliff hunting gull eggs; Mr. Simmons's basket; Bart, Arthur save him; Bruce's heart; boat trip; Arthur drops rope; Bruce collapses ("I'm dying"); boat lost in fog.
6. VI: Search; fog-horn blasts; Corbet anchors; Mr. Long prays; dawn: Antelope back at Grand Pré.
7. VII: Boat drifts; rocky ledge; Arthur leaps with rope; lobster and shrimp cooked in stones; camp on island.
8. VIII: Camp built (spruce, maple poles, sassafras roots); signal staff; lobster boredom.
9. IX: Gulls' eggs; Bart shoots "wild goose" (actually domestic); Denny O'Rafferty; rescue of Bart's group.
10. X: Phil's omelet failures; Phil signals with red shirt on tree; schooner returns; O'Rafferty home; hatchet gift.
11. XI: Pratt's Cove; feast spoiled by Sammy and Johnny (ate stores); Captain Pratt's wood-pile; sing "Bingo."
12. XII: Anchor broken; search; Pat catches duck (Johnnie) and pig (Sammy); Pat's raw-clam poisoning sequence; Pat throws minerals in mud.
13. XIII: Adrift on schooner; Bart steers into mud/rocks; "Bart confesses."
14. XIV: Shovel-mouth shark fight (Bruce, Bart, Arthur); sculpin in stomach; waiting for tide.
15. XV: Clams ("pison" in May); Mrs. Pratt's medicine list; boys dosed.
16. XVI: Schooner sighting; drift off again; Bart fires pistol; rescued by fisherman's boat with Mr. Long.
17. XVII: Reunion; Long reprimands ("Jonahs").
18–19: Pat's confession of tossing minerals; Mr. Long searches flats; clam-shell found by Bogud.
20: Mate woken with cold water; drift; Corbet on babby; "Flying Dutchman."
21: Long lands at Blomidon ("victim"); Corbet's compass theory.
22: Calm; songs (Uncle Ned, Bart's song "Auld Lang Syne"); wind returns; grounded on mud at Grand Pré.
23: Mud crossing; Phil loses boot; quicksand gully; Cornwallis River swim (Bart & Bruce; Bruce's heart "doldrum"); arrival; Solomon's welcome, "Grand Panjandrum" speech; feast. THE END.

## BOOK 2 of 2: "Adele Doring of the Sunnyside Club" by Grace May North (Lothrop, Lee & Shepard, 1919; Gutenberg #62151). Dedicated to Margaret Edna Rock and happy girls 10–15. Illustrated by Florence Liley Young.

### The Sunny Seven (Sunnyside Club)
- **Adele Doring** (president; 13 in Ch. 7; Giant Father = "Heart's Desire"; mother "Adorable Mother"/"mumsie"; brother **Jack Doring** (leader of Jolly Pirates, "Pirate the Terrible"); cook **Kate** (Irish, "Colleen"); horse **Firefly** (black pony); red cart; Uncle Dixon (traveler; sent blue dragon bowl from Japan girl Wistaria); Uncle Jerry (abroad).
- **Gertrude Willis** (secretary, minister's daughter, gentle, writer).
- **Bertha Angel** (treasurer, practical, 13, tall; brother **Bob Angel**, teasing, delivers groceries; father grocer).
- **Rosamond "Rosie" Wright** (romantic, tatting, timid, "overstudyitis"; wrist-watch).
- **Doris Drexel** (father bank president; grandmother's pillow; hates math).
- **Betty Burd** (youngest, 11→12, petite, dark; widowed mother Mrs. Burd; Uncle George Wainwright, editor; pony "Star" named later; "Betsy Bobbets"; spelling "believe").
- **Peggy Pierce** (father Mr. Pierce owns Bee Hive department store; brother with silver whistle).

### Others
- **Eva Dearman**: orphan, 13 on birthday; father broker lost money; mother died; photo under pillow; later adopted by Uncle Dick (Richard Dearman, Cattle King, Silver Creek/Bar-X Ranch, Arizona/Dry Creek).
- **Amanda Brown**: surly orphan, brown calico; locket with red stones; sings with professor; "Mandy."
- **Mrs. Friend**: orphanage matron.
- **Miss Donovan**: teacher (Seven B).
- **Granny Dorset** (Sarie Dorset, turns 70; wants purple silk dress with lace; grandfather Daniel Doring owned land).
- **Madge Peterson**: artist from city; brother **Everett** (white flannels; sailboat); car "Pigmy"; Roberty-Bob (hunchback; "King's Highway").
- **Eric Brownley** (Kid, foster-father **Jock Henderson**; bear "Little Bear"; pitcher); **Fiddler Fritz**.
- **Miss Grackle (Sally)**, sister Miranda (eloped to Arizona); **Mr. & Mrs. Quigley** (Pa/Ma Quigley; poorhouse; cottage).
- **Grandpa 'Lijah Dally**; **Mr. Wiggin**; **Jenny Dixon**; **Susetta Green**, **Mrs. Melissa Green** (former tavern keeper; Restwell estate; Mr. Cyrus Green).
- **Dick Jensen**, **Lawrence Collins**, **Mr. Drakely** (postman), **Miss Fenton** (art teacher), **Dora Pendleton**, **Miss Kimberly**.

### Key Events (order)
Ch1: Club formed at Pussy-willow meadow; pledge rhyme; Adele president; Gertrude secretary; Bertha treasurer.
Ch2: Log cabin (Secret Sanctum), gift from Giant Father; Miss Donovan, examinations.
Ch3: Scrubbing party; china-closet from orange boxes; house-warming planned.
Ch4: Eva's birthday plan at orphanage; Adele spies Eva crying.
Ch5: Bank stolen (actually moved to Mr. Pierce's safe); purchase of 12 locket necklaces at Bee Hive.
Ch6: Surprise hay-rack; Eva/Amanda necklace; Jenny Dixon insult; Amanda rescued.
Ch7: Birthday feast; Bob & Jack as waiters; "Stories That Girls Like Best" gift.
Ch8: Adele's surprise party at home; desk; Japanese painting of cabin; Rosamond's ring cake.
Ch9: Mother Goose play-house for orphans; Bob delivers box.
Ch10–11: Exams; Betty promoted; pony; vacation; Eva to Adele's home.
Ch12: Fudge party; ghost (whitewashed tree).
Ch13–15: Dryads; Madge; Pine Island; pirates (boys playing "Treasure Island").
Ch16–18: Lake; Little Bear story; fish supper; Eric.
Ch19–21: Art lessons; Amanda's singing; ball game (Eric arrives on horse).
Ch22: "King's Highway" composition by Gertrude.
Ch23–25: New school year; Granny party plans; Miss Grackle visit; Quigleys; miser story.
Ch26: Gold found in fireplace (chipmunk); $1000 deposited; Miss Grackle invites Quigleys to cottage.
Ch27: Surprise party for Granny Dorset (purple silk dress); wolf story (Grandpa Dally); Quigleys move in.
Ch28–30: Susetta; Eva taken as servant; humiliation; Mrs. Friend cannot prevent.
Ch31–33: Uncle Dick arrives; Eva reunited; Amanda invited west; farewell; "Adele Doring on a Ranch" sequel mentioned.
